findings.description: The fixture requirement is not fully locked to the real build_view_state surface. F004 requires one integration path, while F005 can still be satisfied by lower-level baseline tests, leaving Python, JS/TS, Swift/Kotlin, empty, and truncated fixtures unproven through the operator-facing path.
findings.recommendation: Make F005 explicitly drive project registration plus build_view_state for every fixture case, not just the baseline builder.

findings.description: The detector promises build systems, test frameworks, app frameworks, infra, and config surfaces, but the coverage block only names filesystem, package_manifest, imports, runtime, and adr. Those detected evidence classes could be invisible or ambiguously folded into filesystem.
findings.recommendation: Either add explicit coverage statuses for build_system, test_framework, app_framework, infra, and config, or define and test their deterministic mapping into existing evidence types.

findings.description: The plan ensures baseline graph data is emitted, but it does not explicitly protect the existing render-truth path from filtering out low-confidence unresolved edges, filesystem/config nodes, or scan_truncated markers before the user sees them.
findings.recommendation: Add an acceptance check against the final build_view_state/render payload that low-confidence edges, tier-0 nodes, and truncation markers survive unchanged.

findings.description: Overall rollup and honest confidence ceilings remain underspecified. Runtime is a tier-3 non-goal, ADR may be absent, and scans may truncate, but the exact deterministic rules for limited versus partial versus covered are not locked.
findings.recommendation: Define rollup rules before implementation, including how absent runtime, absent ADR, heuristic-only imports, parser-backed imports, and scan_truncated affect the overall status.
